items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: During the week, Harold Baker, who was Mary Lou's ole man, had a dispute with Mary and gave Andy his notice...

ctx.x: During the week, Harold Baker, who was Mary Lou's ole man, had a dispute with Mary and gave Andy his notice and said that he was going to stay in St. Louis. I think that he had over accepted to work with some orchestra. So Andy had contacted his booking agency which was Joe Glaser, the one that booked Armstrong also, and asked Joe to send him a trumpet player to replace Harold. Two days before we closed, a trumpet player named Howard McGhee arrived. Andy called a rehearsal for the next afternoon and when I…

Then arrived the day for us to leave St. Louis and Harold "Shorty Boo" Baker had changed his mind and couldn't stand to let his sweet Mary Lou leave him, and it seems as though Mary Lou may have left the band if Andy hadn't agreed to take Shorty back. Andy didn't want to lose Mary Lou, so he was stuck with four trumpeters because McGhee had been sent to him by Glaser and he was obliged to keep him.

The bus driver stopped a few miles outside of St. Louis to gas up and I wanted to take a look. So I went inside the station and asked one of the attendants if I could use the toilet. From inside of the station, one could see when cars were coming from either direction and this fellow told me that I could go in the toilet, but not stay very long. I wasn't supposed to be seen coming out of the toilet by a white customer.
